q: We simulate a Waterfall-style development cycle covering Requirement, Design, Implementation, and Testing using three LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-Chat, and Claude-3.5Haiku) on 100 Python tasks from the ClassEval benchmark.
r: Include: controlled empirical comparison of multi-agent workflow configurations on the same class-level tasks, relevant to RQ3.

q: Our evaluation reveals a significant gap between current agent capabilities and the demands of industrial mobile development, with the best configurations achieving only a 12% success rate.
r: Include: new benchmark of feature development from PRDs, evaluating Cursor, Codex and Claude Code, with cost and robustness analysis.

q: we propose FeatureBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate agentic coding performance in end-to-end, feature-oriented software development.
r: Include: new benchmark for feature-level development by coding agents with execution-based evaluation.

q: BeyondSWE, a 500-instance benchmark for evaluating code agents beyond singlerepository bug fixing, spanning four representative settings that vary in knowledge scope and resolution scope.
r: Include: new benchmark with cost and token budget analysis, including dependency migration and document-to-repository generation, not only issue repair.

q: The principle of our approach is to hold the functional specification constant while systematically varying the non-functional requirements (i.e., structural constraints).
r: Include: controlled comparison of agents and models on greenfield and feature backend tasks with a new evaluation design.

q: given only API specifications, an agent must re-implement an entire repository such that its behavior matches the original implementation.
r: Include: new benchmark for repository-level generation from scratch with execution-based verification, evaluating several agents and models.

q: SaaSBench, the first benchmark platform designed to evaluate the ability of coding agents to generate and deploy enterprise-level SaaS systems from scratch.
r: Include: new project-level benchmark building SaaS systems from PRDs, with a new dependency-aware evaluation protocol.

q: Each task is run ten times per side of its pair, producing 33 × 2 × 10 = 660 trials in total.
r: Include: controlled minimal-pair evaluation protocol with repetitions and token-footprint metrics for a coding agent on code-change tasks.

q: a natural language description of the specification (ii) visible validation tests that exercise specified features in isolation, and (iii) held-out tests that compose those same features to simulate real-world usage.
r: Include: new benchmark and evaluation method (reward hacking measure) for long-horizon coding agents building software from specifications.

q: a project-scale software-engineering benchmark whose difficulty comes from sustained engineering work rather than isolated patch localization;
r: Include: new project-scale benchmark evaluating 13 agent-model configurations with token and cost data over 1,300 trajectories.
